newsitem.title: GREECE: DAIMLER-BENZ TO BUILD NEW METEORA AIRPORT BY 2000.
newsitem.headline: DAIMLER-BENZ TO BUILD NEW METEORA AIRPORT BY 2000.

text.p: The masterplan for a new airport at Meteora will be presented by Germany's Daimler-Benz Airport Systems, Faulenbach Da Costa Airport Consulting and Meteora Airport SA on February 23.
"The purpose of the new airport is to facilitate air transport of Thessaly residents and contribute to the development of tourism in the area with regular flights," Meteora Airport SA said.
The first phase of construction is budgeted at 10.5 billion drachmas and is expected to employ 300 people, it said.
Daimler-Benz Airport Systems, a subsidiary of Daimler Benz Aerospace will build the airport.
"Access to international commercial centers and cargo services will also help the agricultural economy of Thessaly," the airport company said.
The project is supported by other Greek and foreign companies including Dornier GmbH, Hellenic Aerospace Industry (EAB), Heracles Cements and International Commerce & Financing Corp.
Based on the masterplan, the airport will be delivered in the year 2000 and will feature a runway of 2,450 metres and a taxiway 45-metres wide.
Meteora Airport will also have cargo facilities, a passenger terminal, maintenance hangars and parking facilities for general aviation. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
